svg.title: Analysis Senior Responsible Officer: journey through the playbook
svg.desc: Analysis Senior Responsible Officer: journey through the playbook. Stops run across the top in the order they are met, and this reads one stop at a time. Seven steps on one Business Critical output, from being named to revalidating the designation. Stop 1: You have been named for a piece of Business Critical analysis. In the playbook: Business Critical analysis. What you do there: Be named at scoping, before the analysis starts. Outputs: The register entry, with your name against it. Watch out for: Being named afterwards does not work. Most of the lifecycle has happened. Stop 2: What am I taking responsibility for? In the playbook: The Analysis Senior Responsible Officer. What you do there: Risks across the lifecycle, and suitability for the intended use. Outputs: Nothing recorded yet. Watch out for: You need to be senior enough to carry that. Stop 3: Is the work set up to succeed? In the playbook: Phase 1 Engagement and scoping. What you do there: Confirm the Business Critical status, and the resources and plans for assurance. Outputs: Confirmed resources, and the register entry checked. Watch out for: None. Stop 4: Has the design been governed? In the playbook: Phase 2 Design. What you do there: Confirm design governance has been followed before the analysis starts. Outputs: Design governance confirmed, and recorded. Watch out for: None. Stop 5: The work is running. In the playbook: Phase 3 Analysis. What you do there: Stay aware of progress, and be available to approve at delivery. Outputs: Nothing recorded. Your availability in the schedule. Watch out for: None. Stop 6: Approving it. In the playbook: Phase 4 Delivery and sign-off. What you do there: Approve it as fit for its intended use, before it is used. Outputs: Your approval, recorded with what you confirmed. Watch out for: You shall review the evidence. The Lead Assurer signs off first. Stop 7: Is the designation still right? In the playbook: Phase 5 Review. What you do there: Revalidate the designation annually, and before any reuse for a new purpose. Outputs: The revalidated designation, and the register updated. Watch out for: Reuse is the change most likely to invalidate the original assumptions. The loop: Step 7 loops back to step 2. What review finds is what the next revalidation starts from. Open alongside, at any step: Deciding your assurance level for how the designation was reached. Business Critical analysis for everything that is true only of Business Critical work. Roles and responsibilities for the older titles you will meet this role under. NHSBSA Producing Quality Analysis Playbook. Service design artefacts for workshop use. Seamus Sands for NHSBSA, SOW-DOC053.

2. What am I taking responsibility for?

div.div: Be named at scoping, before the analysis starts.
Risks across the lifecycle, and suitability for the intended use.
Confirm the Business Critical status, and the resources and plans for assurance.
Confirm design governance has been followed before the analysis starts.
Stay aware of progress, and be available to approve at delivery.
Approve it as fit for its intended use, before it is used.
Revalidate the designation annually, and before any reuse for a new purpose.

Nothing recorded. Your availability in the schedule.
Your approval, recorded with what you confirmed.
The revalidated designation, and the register updated.

div.span: What the playbook warns about here

div.div: Being named afterwards does not work. Most of the lifecycle has happened.
You need to be senior enough to carry that.
You shall review the evidence. The Lead Assurer signs off first.
Reuse is the change most likely to invalidate the original assumptions.

div.span: Step 7 loops back to step 2. What review finds is what the next revalidation starts from.
